title: Ayer trabajé mucho
blurbEn: The second past tense, for time that is finished and gone. Regular -ar verbs first — and notice the accent on the last syllable.
body:
Ayer trabajé mucho. Me levanté muy temprano y llegué a la oficina a las ocho.

Por la mañana hablé con tres clientes y preparé un informe largo para mi jefe. Después comí un bocadillo rápido en la calle, cerca del parque.

Por la tarde terminé la presentación y ayudé a Sofía con un problema difícil. Antes de salir revisé los correos otra vez.

Salí de la oficina a las siete y media. Llegué a casa muy cansada, cené algo ligero y me acosté pronto.

Hoy he descansado. Ayer trabajé demasiado.
translationEn:
Yesterday I worked a lot. I got up very early and arrived at the office at eight.

In the morning I spoke with three clients and prepared a long report for my boss. Afterwards I ate a quick sandwich on the street, near the park.

In the afternoon I finished the presentation and helped Sofía with a difficult problem. Before leaving I checked the emails again.

I left the office at half past seven. I got home very tired, had a light dinner and went to bed early.

Today I have rested. Yesterday I worked too much.

trabajé.note: The accent is on the last syllable and it matters: 'trabajo' is I work, 'trabajó' is he worked, 'trabajé' is I worked.

llegué.note: Spelled with 'gu' to keep the hard g sound before -é. 'llegé' would be pronounced differently.

Ayer.note: Finished time. This is the word that forces this tense rather than 'he trabajado'.
